[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L1 gold records for structurally related beta-blockers and other oral drugs report absolute oral bioavailability values of 36-100%, all above the 20% threshold; no voting record supports F below 20%.

L4 records show related beta-blockers have measurable solubility and permeability: labetalol is high-solubility with rat jejunum Peff 2.7e-5 cm/s (C119,C117); sotalol has Caco-2 A-B Papp about 2.9e-6 cm/s (C123,C106); acebutolol has Papp 2.94e-6 cm/s and pH 7 solubility 4.08 mg/mL (C130,C133); atenolol shows intestinal perfusion values in the 0.2-5e-6 cm/s range (C104,C132,C144,C134,C113,C107).

L5 gut-wall records show P-gp efflux does not by itself imply F<20: labetalol is a P-gp substrate with verapamil-sensitive efflux and A-B Papp 5.96e-6 cm/s (C162,C153); sotalol is a P-gp substrate with GG918-sensitive efflux yet L1 records report F approximately 80-100% (C158,C167,C11,C16); atenolol has human jejunal Peff 0.20e-4 cm/s (C151). Low Caco-2 permeability (SAHA, C188) coexists with human F 43% (C23).

L6 hepatic clearance/metabolic stability records do not provide affirmative high first-pass extraction for the query scaffold: beta-blocker-like and thiazole-containing reference molecules show mostly low-to-moderate intrinsic clearance (e.g., denopamine glucuronide CLint 1.6-3.4 µL/min/mg in human/dog/monkey, C249,C240,C225,C238,C203,C235; M1 human microsomal CLint 0.027-0.096 mL/min/mg, C202,C216,C206), and moderate/high clearance records are for structurally unrelated molecules without F outcomes (C215,C224,C230,C245).

No query-specific direct oral bioavailability, absorption, efflux, or hepatic clearance data are available; the high prediction rests on transferable high-F contexts and the absence of affirmative threshold-relevant low-F evidence.

evidence_gaps: No direct query-specific oral bioavailability or IV-comparison data are available.
No query-specific solubility, permeability, P-gp efflux, or hepatic clearance measurements exist.
PEPT1 applicability to the query is inferred from structural analogy only; the query lacks the free carboxylate typical of many PEPT1 substrates.
L6 hepatic clearance records are for reference molecules, not the query; species, assay system, and scaling differ, and no F outcome is attached.
L6 includes a short HLM half-life (13 min) for TJ0711 (C217), but this is for a different aryloxypropanolamine scaffold and is not affirmative low-F evidence for the query.
No affirmative low-F comparator context for the query scaffold was available.
content.decision_summary: L6 hepatic clearance/metabolic stability records are indirect and mixed; they provide no affirmative low-F evidence for the query, and moderate/high clearance records are for unrelated scaffolds without F outcomes. Combined with L1 gold F values of 36-100% for related beta-blockers and L4/L5 absorption/efflux context, F>=20% remains better supported. Prediction high with moderate confidence; decision kept.

You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
